# Release check — v1.2.0, 2026-08-28

The manual pass required by README's "Before publishing" and by
`scripts/prepublish-check.js`. Performed by Claude against pages built from
**this branch's** scaffolds — not pages generated by an earlier version — and
this repository's own map: 66 files, 668 functions, 8 of 8 entry points traced,
16 verified quality findings.

Pages were built by filling each shipped scaffold's tokens the way the prompt
prose instructs, then served over `http://localhost:4319` and opened in headless
Chromium. Every number below was read out of the live document, not out of the
source that produced it.

**Step 4 was not performed — see "Not covered by this pass" at the end. It is
outstanding and a human has to do it before publishing.**

## Step 1 — every page renders

| Page | Scaffold | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | `index.template.html` | Renders. Title `code-flow-skill · code flow`, 4 coverage cells (66 files scanned, 668 functions catalogued, 8 entry points found, 8 flows traced), 8 flow cards |
| `templates_shared_tracers_trace_python_main.html` | `viewer.template.html` | Renders. 40 graph nodes, 194 SVG paths |
| `quality-report.html` | `report.template.html` | Renders. Coverage reads "8 of 8 entry points found were traced", 16 findings, principle chips DRY and KISS |
| `code-flow.html` | `bundle.template.html` | Renders all three in one document: landing lists the same 8 flows, `#/flow/…` opens a graph with the same 40 nodes, `#/report` reaches the same 16 findings |

No page errors on any of the four. The one console 404 seen on `index.html` is
Chromium's automatic `/favicon.ico` probe against a bare directory server: the
scaffold contains no `<link>` and no `src=` at all, so it requests nothing.

Two things this release changed were confirmed in the rendered page rather than
in the template source:

- **Clean detectors are named.** The report and the bundle both print
  `Ran and found nothing: unreached, single-responsibility,
  interface-segregation, dependency-cycle, shallow-module, pass-through,
  internals-coupled-test, open-closed, liskov-substitution`. On a report where
  every SOLID and DEPTH detector is clean, that is the difference between
  "checked, nothing found" and a silence that reads as "never checked".
- **No fragment-id references survive.** The flow page has 0 `<marker>` elements
  and 0 `url(#` references in its whole serialized DOM, which is what keeps a
  generated page from being quarantined by corporate mail gateways.

## Step 2 — corrupted data shows the error card, not a blank page

The opening `{` was deleted from each page's embedded JSON block. Each result
was confirmed unparseable by `json.loads` **before** loading, so the check could
not pass vacuously — the v1.1.0 pass threw out a first attempt that had
corrupted a character inside a string, which leaves JSON valid.

| Page | Shown | Page still drawn |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | `Invalid JSON in #index-data` + parser message + the `<\/` tip | 18,346 chars |
| `templates_shared_tracers_trace_python_main.html` | `Invalid JSON in #flow-data` + parser message + tip | 88,793 chars |
| `quality-report.html` | `Invalid JSON in #report-data` + parser message + tip | 31,492 chars |
| `code-flow.html` | `Bundle failed to load — Invalid JSON in bundle data:` + parser message | 451,053 chars |

## Step 3 — links navigate

Clicked as real anchors, with `location.pathname` and `document.title` read
afterwards:

- `index.html` → flow card → `/templates_shared_tracers_trace_c_family_main.html`, 76 nodes drawn
- that flow page → `Flows` → `/index.html`, 8 flow cards again
- `quality-report.html` → `Flows` → `/index.html`
- `index.html` → quality link → `/quality-report.html`, 16 findings

Nothing calls `preventDefault` on the flow card: a listener that recorded
`defaultPrevented` after the event had bubbled past every handler read `false`,
so the navigation is the anchor's own rather than script-driven.

## Step 5 — a user theme applies in both modes

`--accent` was **uncommented in both blocks** of a copy of the shipped
`theme.css`, with a different value per block, exactly as a user edits
`.code-flow/theme.css`:

```css
:root{ --accent:#ff2d95; }
[data-theme="light"]{ --accent:#008b45; }
```

Read from the live document, and compared against the same page built from the
stock theme so the check shows a pixel changing rather than a variable
resolving:

| Theme | `data-theme` | `.coverage-banner h2` computed colour | |
|---|---|---|---|
| stock | dark | `rgb(145, 132, 217)` | built-in |
| stock | light | `rgb(93, 82, 148)` | built-in |
| user | dark | `rgb(255, 45, 149)` | `#ff2d95` ✓ |
| user | light | `rgb(0, 139, 69)` | `#008b45` ✓ |

Both blocks matter: they have equal specificity, so a theme that set only
`:root` would apply its dark colours in light mode and look like a broken
toggle.

## Step 6 — the tracers against code this repository did not write

The suites run the tracers against fixtures this repository wrote, which prove
the contract and prove nothing about the heuristics.

| Tracer | Corpus | Files | Functions | Call edges | Entry points | Components |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trace_python.py` | CPython 3.11 standard library | 670 | 14,720 | 16,887 | 34 | — |
| `trace_typescript.mjs` | PrimeVue 5.0.1 | 820 | 5,817 | 3,381 | 0 | **423** |
| `trace_typescript.mjs` | TypeScript 5.x compiler | 9 | 20,892 | **80,827** | 1 | 8 |
| `trace_rust.py` | serde_json 1.x and its 10 dependencies, vendored | 339 | 6,302 | 7,433 | 6 | — |
| `trace_java.py` | Gson, Commons Lang 3, Guava, JUnit console, picocli | 1,000 | 18,131 | 15,424 | 2 | — |
| `trace_c_family.py` | `/usr/include` | 4,145 | 12,765 | 6,387 | 0 | — |

`componentsFound` is the number the checklist says to sanity-check against what
the app has: **423 components against PrimeVue's 416 `.vue` files**, the excess
being components declared outside a single-file component.

The two zeroes were checked rather than accepted:

- **Java, before adding a CLI corpus, found 0 entry points** across Gson,
  Commons Lang and Guava. Two files matched `static void main` — both inside
  Javadoc, which the tracer masks. Adding JUnit's console launcher and picocli
  took it to exactly 2, at `ConsoleLauncher.java:32` and `AutoComplete.java:72`,
  which are the only two real `main` methods in the whole corpus. Five files
  match the text; three of those are documentation.
- **C family finds 0 entry points in `/usr/include`**, correct for a header
  tree. The one `int main(` in it is inside a `#define` in `cursesapp.h`, and
  preprocessor lines are masked.

The last part of step 6 — build a whole map from tracer output rather than by
re-reading — was run with `scripts/build-map.py` against PrimeVue. **It did not
finish; see below.**

## What this pass found

### Id collisions on ordinary real-world code

`scripts/build-map.py` asserts that ids are unique across the merged catalog.
It fired. Measured across all six corpora:

| Corpus | Functions | Duplicated ids |
|---|---|---|
| CPython standard library | 14,720 | **158** |
| `/usr/include` | 12,765 | **106** |
| PrimeVue | 5,817 | **107** |
| Gson + Commons Lang + Guava + JUnit + picocli | 18,131 | **42** |
| TypeScript compiler | 20,892 | 4 |
| serde_json and dependencies | 6,302 | 0 |

This is not a minified-code curiosity. Three separate mechanisms, each of them
ordinary:

1. **`derive_id` folds two distinct names onto one id, and `assign_ids` counts
   names.** The `_l<line>` suffix is applied when a file defines *the same name*
   twice, but the id comes from a slug that lowercases and replaces everything
   outside `[a-z0-9_]`. So the pairs below are different names that derive one
   id, are counted as unique, and get no suffix:
   - Python `__add__` and `add`, `__abs__` and `abs`, `__hash__` and `_hash` —
     every dunder collides with its plain-named counterpart. `_pydecimal.py`
     alone contributes dozens.
   - Java `Builder` the constructor and `builder()` the static factory. That is
     the builder pattern, in `DiffBuilder`, `ReflectionDiffBuilder` and others.
   - C++ `__waiter` and `~__waiter` — **every class with a destructor**.
   - Case: `_M_x` and `_M_X` in `chrono_io.h`, `F` and `f` in bundled JS.
2. **Two definitions on one line.** 105 of PrimeVue's 107 and 45 of
   `/usr/include`'s 106. `_l<line>` cannot separate them, and no record carries
   a column.
3. **Two file paths folding to one slug.** 10 in the standard library, all of
   the `distutils/_msvccompiler.py` versus `distutils/msvccompiler.py` shape:
   the leading `_` becomes a separator and collapses into the one before it.
   This one is not fixable by a rule that decides collisions "from the file's
   own contents", which is what the id rule documents in all four host
   templates.

The consequence is not cosmetic. An id is what the call graph refers to a
function by, and `/code-flow.quality` computes `unreached` by subtracting
reached ids from catalogued ids. Two functions sharing an id means reaching
either one reports both as reached — so a genuinely unreachable function is
silently absent from the findings, which is the exact failure mode
`detectorsSkipped` and the "ran and found nothing" line exist to prevent.

**This is unresolved as of this pass.** It predates this release — the rule has
been this way since the tracers landed — and fixing class 3 means changing a
rule stated verbatim in four host templates.

## Not covered by this pass

- **Step 4 — loading the skills on a real host.** This environment has no
  Claude Code, Copilot, Codex or Antigravity surface to install into and no way
  to see a slash menu. Nothing here observed a host discovering
  `code-flow-map`, listing it once rather than twice on Copilot, or reporting
  no frontmatter error. That step is untouched and still owed before publishing.
- **A real Angular or React application.** PrimeVue exercises the Vue
  single-file-component path against 416 real components; the React, Angular
  and Svelte passes were exercised only by this repository's fixtures.
